identity.title: [v0.92][WP-04.16a] Secure and durably persist three-voter OpenRaft transport

values.summary: Design the encrypted transport and storage transaction, implement the bounded substrate, prove adversarial transport and crash recovery, obtain independent review, and publish one reviewed PR for #191.

steps.action: Freeze existing-transport identity, authority-derived topology, framing, retry-cache and storage transaction invariants from current source.
Extend the authoritative encrypted transport and implement crash-safe OpenRaft durable stores without higher-level authority policy.
Add exact three-voter, authorized-overlap, retry/conflict, checkpoint rollback, membership parity, corruption, injected-failure, path and restart tests.
Seal proof, resolve independent review, publish and shepherd CI; do not merge without operator authority.

invariants: No plaintext Raft RPC is accepted in production mode and no parallel transport authority is created outside distributed/transport.rs.
Every route comes from exact MembershipState and AuthorityMembership parity; caller routing hints cannot create a voter.
No OpenRaft callback makes live state visible before its own durable transaction and external checkpoint reconciliation complete.
Exact retries return a durable cached response; conflicting replay is never redispatched.

The trusted deployment bootstrap owns configured certificate roots and the externally retained membership commitment; untrusted transport, RPC, and routing inputs cannot mint application authority, and no secret enters retained evidence.
risks: OpenRaft storage callbacks can make atomic ordering easy to overstate.
Certificate rotation or restart replay state can diverge from transport identity.
Network fault tests can accidentally prove only signed plaintext instead of encryption.
stop_conditions: The current transport module cannot provide a domain-bound Quinn/rustls session without widening to an explicitly reviewed transport path.
A storage callback contract makes fail-atomic application impossible without a separate bounded storage issue.
Focused proof cannot distinguish encrypted production traffic from a test-only adapter.
